CCA-000.details: This wraps an error from npm, tar, or another upstream tool invoked by create-catalyst-app. See the printed upstream message for the actual cause.
CCA-000.suggestedAction: Read the upstream error message printed above and fix the underlying issue.

CCA-001.details: The project name is not a valid npm package name.
CCA-001.suggestedAction: Choose a project name that is a valid npm package name and try again.

CCA-002.details: A file or directory with the project name already exists in the current directory.
CCA-002.suggestedAction: Choose a different project name, or remove/rename the existing directory.

CCA-005.details: The -y/--yes flag does not accept a non-boolean value.
CCA-005.suggestedAction: Use -y or --yes with no value to accept defaults.

CCA-006.details: npm pack could not produce the tarball used to scaffold the new project.
CCA-006.suggestedAction: Check your npm registry access/network connection and try again.

CCA-007.details: The packed tarball could not be extracted into the new project directory.
CCA-007.suggestedAction: Ensure the target directory is writable and try again.

CCA-008.details: Downloading, installing, or configuring the MCP server failed.
CCA-008.suggestedAction: Check your network connection and re-run `catalyst-mcp` inside the project.

CCA-009.details: The scaffolded project already contains a .gitignore file.
CCA-009.suggestedAction: Remove or rename the existing .gitignore before running again, or ignore this warning.

PREFLIGHT-022.message: The build is stale: config/config.json changed since it was built
PREFLIGHT-022.details: PUBLIC_STATIC_ASSET_URL, PUBLIC_STATIC_ASSET_PATH and the CLIENT_ENV_VARIABLES values are inlined into the bundles at build time, so serving this build would use the old values.
PREFLIGHT-022.suggestedAction: Run `npm run build` again, then `npm run serve`.

PROCESS-001.message: preServerInit threw an error during server startup
PROCESS-001.details: The preServerInit hook failed. Note: server startup currently continues despite this error (tracked separately as a fix — see issue #298); this code only identifies which hook failed.
PROCESS-001.suggestedAction: Fix the error thrown inside your preServerInit hook (see the cause above).

PROCESS-002.message: A user-defined hook threw an error
PROCESS-002.details: A user-defined hook (e.g. onRouteMatch, onFetcherError, onServerError) threw. It was caught so the SSR pipeline keeps running; see the cause above for which hook and why.
PROCESS-002.suggestedAction: Fix the error thrown inside the hook (see the cause above).

BUNDLE-000.message: Build failed in an upstream bundler step
BUNDLE-000.details: This is a wrapper around an error from Vite/Rollup or another upstream build tool. See the printed upstream code/message for the actual cause — catalyst-core does not reinterpret it.
BUNDLE-000.suggestedAction: Read the upstream error message/code printed above and fix the underlying issue.

IOS-000.message: iOS build failed in an upstream toolchain step
IOS-000.details: This wraps an error from Xcode/CocoaPods. See the printed upstream output for the cause.
IOS-000.suggestedAction: Read the upstream Xcode/CocoaPods error printed above and fix the underlying issue.

IOS-001.message: Could not find an installed iOS Simulator app
IOS-001.details: Neither DeviceHub.app (Xcode 27+, bundle id com.apple.dt.Devices) nor the legacy Simulator.app (bundle id com.apple.iphonesimulator) is installed under Xcode's Contents/Applications. The simulator itself may still boot headlessly via simctl, but catalyst-core cannot open or focus its window.
IOS-001.suggestedAction: Confirm a full Xcode.app (not just Command Line Tools) is installed and selected via xcode-select -p, then reopen it once from Spotlight so macOS registers its app bundle.

IOS-002.message: Full Xcode is not installed or selected
IOS-002.details: setupEmulator:ios and buildApp:ios need Xcode.app, not only the Command Line Tools. xcode-select -p does not point inside an Xcode app bundle, so there is no simulator, iOS SDK or app-building xcodebuild.
IOS-002.suggestedAction: Install Xcode from the Mac App Store, then run sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer.

IOS-003.details: The Xcode licence has not been accepted or its first-launch components are not installed, so xcodebuild and simctl refuse to run. Both steps need an administrator password, so they only run after a yes in an interactive terminal.
IOS-003.suggestedAction: Run sudo xcodebuild -license accept and sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch, then retry.

IOS-004.details: Xcode has no available iOS simulator runtime, so there is no simulator to create or boot. The runtime is a download of several gigabytes and is only fetched after a yes in an interactive terminal or with --yes.
IOS-004.suggestedAction: Run catalyst setupEmulator:ios in a terminal or with --yes, or run xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS yourself.

IOS-005.details: public/icon.png becomes the app's single 1024x1024 universal AppIcon, so it must be a PNG file, square, and at least 1024 by 1024 pixels.
IOS-005.suggestedAction: Replace public/icon.png with a square PNG of at least 1024x1024 pixels, or add the sized icons in public/ios/appIcons.

IOS-006.details: App Store Connect rejects app icons with an alpha channel (ITMS-90717). public/icon.png has an alpha channel or a transparency chunk, which fails an iOS release build. Debug builds only warn.
IOS-006.suggestedAction: Export public/icon.png without an alpha channel (flatten it onto a solid background), then rebuild.

ANDROID-000.message: Android build failed in an upstream toolchain step
ANDROID-000.details: This wraps an error from Gradle. See the printed upstream output for the cause.
ANDROID-000.suggestedAction: Read the upstream Gradle error printed above and fix the underlying issue.

ANDROID-001.message: Timed out waiting for the Android emulator to boot
ANDROID-001.details: buildApp:android launched the configured AVD but it did not appear in `adb devices` or did not finish booting (sys.boot_completed=1 and init.svc.bootanim=stopped) within the timeout.
ANDROID-001.suggestedAction: Try booting the AVD manually first (emulator -avd <name>) to see the actual startup error, check available disk space/RAM, or increase the emulator's cold-boot allowance if the device is unusually slow.

ANDROID-002.message: Release build points at a local or private host
ANDROID-002.details: The release start URL, built from WEBVIEW_CONFIG.release merged over WEBVIEW_CONFIG (useHttps, LOCAL_IP, port), names localhost, a loopback, RFC 1918, link-local or .local address, or this machine's own address. Users' devices cannot reach it, so the store build would open on an error page.
ANDROID-002.suggestedAction: Set WEBVIEW_CONFIG.release.LOCAL_IP (and port/useHttps) to your production host, or set WEBVIEW_CONFIG.release.allowPrivateHost to true for an internal app on a private network.

ANDROID-003.message: Release build has no build number
ANDROID-003.details: Google Play needs a new, higher versionCode for every upload. None was given through --build-number, the CATALYST_BUILD_NUMBER environment variable, or WEBVIEW_CONFIG.android.version.buildNumber.
ANDROID-003.suggestedAction: Pass --build-number <n>, set CATALYST_BUILD_NUMBER in CI, or set WEBVIEW_CONFIG.android.version.buildNumber.

ANDROID-004.details: The build number becomes the app's versionCode, which must be a whole number from 1 to 2100000000 (the largest value Google Play accepts).
ANDROID-004.suggestedAction: Use a whole number from 1 to 2100000000 that is higher than the last one you uploaded.

ANDROID-005.message: No upload key for the release build
ANDROID-005.details: A release build signs the app bundle with the app's upload key. None was found at credentials/android/upload.jks, android.signing.storeFile or CATALYST_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64, and a new key is only created after a yes in an interactive terminal.
ANDROID-005.suggestedAction: Run the release build once in a terminal to create credentials/android/upload.jks, or in CI set CATALYST_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 and CATALYST_ANDROID_STORE_PASSWORD (plus CATALYST_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS and CATALYST_ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD when they differ from the defaults).

ANDROID-006.message: Upload key settings are incomplete or wrong
ANDROID-006.details: An upload keystore was found but cannot be used: its file is missing, no store password was given, or keytool rejected the password or alias.
ANDROID-006.suggestedAction: Check credentials/android/keystore.properties, or the CATALYST_ANDROID_* environment variables, against the keystore.

ANDROID-007.details: Gradle and the Android SDK tools need JDK 17 or newer. None was found in JAVA_HOME, /usr/libexec/java_home or Android Studio's bundled runtime, and installing one with Homebrew needs a yes in an interactive terminal on macOS.
ANDROID-007.suggestedAction: Install JDK 17 or newer (macOS: brew install --cask zulu@17; Linux: your distribution's openjdk-17-jdk package) and set JAVA_HOME, or run catalyst setupEmulator:android in a terminal to install it.

ANDROID-008.message: Android SDK setup needs your confirmation
ANDROID-008.details: setupEmulator:android found Android SDK pieces to download (command-line tools, packages or a system image), an emulator to create, or SDK licences to accept. Downloads only happen after a yes in an interactive terminal or with --yes, and licences are only accepted interactively or with --accept-licenses.
ANDROID-008.suggestedAction: Run catalyst setupEmulator:android in a terminal, or pass --yes to allow the downloads and --accept-licenses to accept the Android SDK licences (for CI).

ANDROID-009.message: Could not install the Android command-line tools
ANDROID-009.details: The pinned Android command-line tools archive could not be downloaded, did not match its published SHA-256, or could not be unpacked into <sdk>/cmdline-tools/latest.
ANDROID-009.suggestedAction: Check your network or proxy and retry, or download the command-line tools from https://developer.android.com/studio#command-tools and unzip them so that <sdk>/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager exists.

ANDROID-010.details: public/icon.png becomes the Android launcher icon when public/android/appIcons has no per-density icons, so it must be a PNG file, square, and at least 1024 by 1024 pixels.
ANDROID-010.suggestedAction: Replace public/icon.png with a square PNG of at least 1024x1024 pixels, or add per-density icons in public/android/appIcons.

RUNTIME-NATIVE-013.details: The native bridge is not available or not initialized

RUNTIME-NATIVE-014.details: This feature is not supported on the current platform
RUNTIME-NATIVE-014.suggestedAction: Try using an alternative method or device

RUNTIME-NATIVE-015.details: An internal error occurred while processing the request
RUNTIME-NATIVE-015.suggestedAction: Try again or contact support if the problem persists

RUNTIME-NATIVE-016.details: Camera hardware is not available or accessible

RUNTIME-NATIVE-017.details: Camera is being used by another application
RUNTIME-NATIVE-017.suggestedAction: Close other camera apps and try again

RUNTIME-NATIVE-018.details: The native platform invoked WebBridge.callback() with an interface name that isn't recognized.
RUNTIME-NATIVE-018.suggestedAction: Check the interface name against the registered NATIVE_CALLBACKS list; this usually indicates a native/JS version mismatch.

RUNTIME-NATIVE-019.message: No handler registered for this bridge interface
RUNTIME-NATIVE-019.details: Native sent a callback for this interface, but your webview hasn't registered a handler for it yet.
RUNTIME-NATIVE-019.suggestedAction: Call WebBridge.register() for this interface before native calls arrive.

RUNTIME-NATIVE-020.message: A registered bridge callback handler threw
RUNTIME-NATIVE-020.details: The JS handler registered for this native callback interface threw an error while processing the callback.
RUNTIME-NATIVE-020.suggestedAction: Fix the error thrown inside the registered handler (see the cause above).

RUNTIME-NATIVE-021.details: WebBridge.register() was called with a non-function callback or an unrecognized interface name.
RUNTIME-NATIVE-021.suggestedAction: Pass a function as the callback and a valid interface name from NATIVE_CALLBACKS.

RUNTIME-NATIVE-022.details: WebBridge.init() was called outside a browser environment (no `window` available).
RUNTIME-NATIVE-022.suggestedAction: Call WebBridge.init() in a browser environment, before using bridge features.

AI-000.details: This is a wrapper around a non-2xx response or thrown error from the upstream AI provider (OpenAI/Gemini). See the printed upstream status/message for the actual cause — catalyst-ai does not reinterpret it.
AI-000.suggestedAction: Read the upstream provider error printed above and fix the underlying issue (auth, rate limit, invalid request).

AI-001.details: AI_CONFIG.enabled is not set to true.
AI-001.suggestedAction: Set AI_CONFIG.enabled=true in your environment configuration.

AI-002.details: The requested provider is unknown, or has no apiKey configured in AI_CONFIG.providers.
AI-002.suggestedAction: Add the provider's apiKey to AI_CONFIG.providers, or use a configured provider.

AI-003.details: The request body is missing a non-empty messages array, or no model could be resolved.
AI-003.suggestedAction: Pass a non-empty messages array, and either a model or a provider defaultModel.

AI-004.details: window.NativeBridge.initAI or window.WebBridge was not found when useNativeAI mounted.
AI-004.suggestedAction: Update catalyst-core to >=0.2.0, add the native AI module, and call WebBridge.init() before mounting useNativeAI.

AI-005.details: generate() was called before the native side reported a ready stream URL (initAI has not fired ON_AI_READY yet).
AI-005.suggestedAction: Wait for modelReady to become true before calling generate().

AI-006.details: The native AI HTTP endpoint returned a non-ok status or reported an error in its response body.
AI-006.suggestedAction: See the cause above for the native-reported status/message.

AI-007.details: The native platform invoked ON_AI_ERROR — a failure during model load, init, or inference on the native side, not an HTTP request made by this JS code.
AI-007.suggestedAction: See the cause above for the native-reported message.

AI-008.details: Constructing the module Worker for in-browser AI failed — module workers may be unsupported in this browser.
AI-008.suggestedAction: Use a browser with module Worker support, or fall back to useCloudAI/useNativeAI.

AI-009.details: The in-browser AI worker threw during model load or generation (e.g. all device backends failed, or an uncaught exception). See the cause above for the worker's reported message.
AI-009.suggestedAction: Check that the model is compatible with this browser/device, or use useCloudAI/useNativeAI instead.

RUNTIME-WEB-001.details: An error was thrown while streaming or rendering the document on the server. This may originate from app code, a third-party dependency, or catalyst-core itself — see the cause above for the actual error.
RUNTIME-WEB-001.suggestedAction: See the cause above for the error thrown during rendering.

RUNTIME-WEB-002.details: An error was thrown while executing a route's serverFetcher function(s). This may originate from app code, a third-party dependency, or catalyst-core itself — see the cause above for the actual error.
RUNTIME-WEB-002.suggestedAction: See the cause above for the error thrown inside serverFetcher.

RUNTIME-WEB-003.details: An error was thrown while executing the app-level serverSideFunction hook. This may originate from app code, a third-party dependency, or catalyst-core itself — see the cause above for the actual error.
RUNTIME-WEB-003.suggestedAction: See the cause above for the error thrown inside serverSideFunction.

RUNTIME-WEB-004.details: An unhandled error reached the top level of the SSR request handler. This may originate from app code, a third-party dependency, or catalyst-core itself — see the cause above for the actual error.
RUNTIME-WEB-004.suggestedAction: See the cause above for the underlying error.
